newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks unmoved at open but NAB dives.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks unmoved at open but NAB dives.

text.p: The Australian share market was steady at the open on Friday with a firmer resources sector compensating for a bank sector that again attracted sellers.
The All Ordinaries index was steady at 2525.0.

Bank sector leader National Australia Bank suffered most, losing over one percent to A$17.90, although all the big four banks lost ground as traders accepted that margin pressures in the popular sector were likely to intensify.

"It's been a fast ride for them but it looks like profit expectations will have to be adjusted," said a dealer at a Sydney-based investment bank, alluding to sensational share price rises seen in the sector over the past few weeks.
The rest of the market was largely ignored in terms of activity, although the large miners were stronger, overcoming the 1.2 percent fall from the bank grouping.
Further gains by RTZ Corp Plc underpinned CRA, it added 15.3 cents to A$20.18, while fresh highs from copper boosted bellwether BHP, up 17 cents at A$18.30.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about two to one, while about 47 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
